assistant|powwow_game_stick_game: Traditional game played with stick markers and a bowl; game of chance and skill where players guess the location of the marked stick
assistant|powwow_game_hand_games: Traditional gambling game with two teams; played with bones or sticks, teams guess which hand hides the bone or stick
assistant|powwow_game_drum_dance_competi: Popular powwow feature; drum groups compete for best rhythm and dancers compete on style and skill
assistant|powwow_game_indian_relay: Fast-paced horse racing event with multiple riders and horse exchanges; goal is completing a circuit in the shortest time
assistant|powwow_game_lacrosse: Traditional game played with a ball and long-handled stick; points scored by hitting the opposing team's goal
assistant|powwow_game_double_ball: Fast-paced game of catching and throwing a small ball with two sticks; points scored by hitting a goal post
assistant|powwow_game_hoop_dance: Traditional dance with intricate movements using multiple hoops, often performed by skilled dancers at powwows
assistant|powwow_highlight: Drum and dance competition attracts the largest crowds and is considered the highlight of a powwow; Indian Relay and lacrosse are also exhilarating
assistant|powwow_gathering_of_nations: One of the largest powwows in North America, takes place in Albuquerque, New Mexico
assistant|powwow_denver_march: Held each spring at the Colorado State Fairgrounds in Denver; showcases history and traditions of the region's indigenous tribes
assistant|powwow_black_hills: One of the longest-running powwows in South Dakota, held annually in Rapid City
assistant|powwow_stanford: Held at Stanford University in California; one of the most well-attended powwows on the West Coast
assistant|powwow_united_tribes: Takes place in Bismarck, North Dakota during the first weekend of September; one of the premier powwows in the United States
assistant|powwow_tip_attire: Dress appropriately - traditional Native American clothing or casual attire; avoid clothing with offensive images or slogans
assistant|powwow_tip_shoes: Wear comfortable shoes as you may be standing or walking for an extended period
assistant|powwow_tip_seating: Bring a comfortable chair or blanket to sit on, as seating may be limited
assistant|powwow_tip_sun_protection: Bring sunscreen and a hat to protect from the sun, as powwows may be held outdoors
assistant|powwow_tip_etiquette: Be respectful and attentive; avoid taking pictures without permission and be mindful of surroundings
assistant|powwow_tip_cash: Bring cash, as some powwows have vendors selling Native American crafts, food, and souvenirs
assistant|powwow_tip_hydration: Bring a water bottle to stay hydrated
